I am a bridge engineer and I love this picture. I have a copy of it pinned to my cubicle wall. It is a great demonstration of some really important basic concepts.
I feel like I'm missing something, could you maybe briefly explain what's happening here?

Ok. So basic idea the man in the middle is being held up by the weight of the blocks on either side of the picture. The men on either side are able to hold him up with little effort because their arms are in tension and the rods that they are holding on to (as well as their torsos) are in compression. I think of the men on either side as balances. Each of them are in balance because they are holding blocks on one side and half of the center mans weight on the other.

A lot of bridge engineering is learning to balance loads to your advantage. You can brute force a lot of designs by making the beams or truss members larger, but that is more expensive. It is much more elegant, simple and cost effective to use geometry and material properties to your advantage. Why build a monster truss when you can have some dead weight (blocks in this case) do the work for you.
